entry.title: May Journal: Throwback
entry.content:
It has been a year since the Dear Eveline challenge ends. That was a fun one. My third canonical album basically served as an exercise to compose one song each month for a year. I ended up having 13 songs with various styles and varying degree of effort put on the respective “music videos”, depending on how busy I was.

If I have to pick a favorite (in this particular order), here are my proudest works:

  1. Christmas Eve: It was supposed to be titled something else but for OSINT mitigation reasons (my top reason for not disclosing information) I quickly changed the title. It’s nice that I got to upload that when it actually was Christmas Eve. This song reminds me a lot of late night Christmas joy, where the weather is just perfect; not too cold so it’s still warm enough outside. You’d go and explore the festive city at night, passing along strangers on the street. I have a soft spot for after night sceneries, the calmness and emptiness of places late at night. That’s what it reminds me of. Less of the cultural/religious background of Christmas Eve, but more of that after hours feeling I get on that time of the year.
  2. End Credits (Outro): Surprisingly the bonus track gets a second place on my favorite list. This song could’ve been more though, especially on the visual side. I was learning about Computer Graphics, especially how computers render 3D scenes using maths, or commonly abstracted using Blender. In fact, the cover art was made using Blender! I did not have enough time and energy to learn 3D animation from 0 and upload a 3D music video. This is wild to say because I have the exact same plan few months ago for a song planned to be released on the next Friday the 13th (which is June 13th this year). I haven’t made any significant progress towards that music vidoe :D!!
  3. Impermanence: Perfect title, good album opener, and a completely different style that for some reasons work well for my taste. Impermanence as a word is also the lesson that keeps ringing in my head the past few years. Could’ve been mixed better though, that’s why it’s on the 3rd place.

Honorable mention would go to One In A Million for the classic reason that I could’ve done better. The song was suppose to be released in November 2023 but I made the last minute decision to partner up with my friend instead for the cover art. It took her a while to finish, but that gave the perfect opportunity for me to release the song in February 2024. Just know that the month is special for me and the person I made One In A Million for.

My thought process on the composition of that song was to basically try to emulate A House In Nebraska by Ethel Cain. Why? Because that song was stuck in my head. If you can’t figure it out, it’s the part my song where a guitar lead suddenly appears over a slow beating drum in the background. Huge emphasis on trying to emulate there. If you don’t know it yet, I use LMMS as my DAW since it’s the only FOSS (and intuitive enough to use) DAW that could run on Linux. Yes, I use Linux, entry 2 and 19 should make it clear that I’m a paranoid freak but anyway. LMMS, DAW, not really ideal for recording emotional, slow burn, songs. Most of the default synths are 8-bit, chiptune-y, game soundtrack synths. I did not own a proper recording equipment when I made that song. So it is what it is, but hey, I’m still proud of it.

Reminder that the album is free to download over on Bandcamp.

entry.title: May Journal: This Is Not Enough

link.title: May Journal: This Is Not Enough

entry.content:
If you could associate a song with the impermanence of human relationship, what would it be?

My personal answer is This Is Not Enough by Hammock.

I think I mentioned that song before. It’s in B major, 3/4 time signature, the chord progression is pretty simple. It’s your usual I - IV - vi - V but they way it’s arranged makes it very beautiful and special to me. The instrumental break near the end is just top notch. I’m always lost having this scenario in my head where flashes of memories spent with my loved ones just play like a movie reel, as if I’m going to fucking die lmao.

Hey, good song. I recommend it.

entry.title: May Journal: Faith, Loyalty, and Trust

link.title: May Journal: Faith, Loyalty, and Trust

entry.content:
Paradoxically I think the most faithful, loyal, and trustworthy person asks the most questions. I think the person you should trust in a crisis should be someone who’s most doubtful. A personal rule of thumb is if someone seems to be so optimistic and believing of a product or solution, run. I think an ethical expert knows better that their solution is not perfect. The more confident you are with something, the more doubtful I am with it. This isn’t something new that everyone just realized, I just happen to give it a proper thought today.

Trust is a big scary word. In a paranoid sense, who do you trust with your personal data online when your behavior has been commodified and used by a few rich oligarchs to control the narrative of the world? In a personal sense, what happens if you let your walls down, be vulnerable be naked and be awkward?

99% of the time, the answer to the personal sense of trust is nothing. 50% maybe it’ll make you happier and more fulfilled. But in a crisis, what if, what if the remaining 1% happens? What kind of mitigation steps do you have? What is your threat model? What are you willing to lose? To what extent are you willing to risk it all, for security? For a sense of stability?

Even if it’s a lost cause, will you stay with the sinking ship? Will you steer the wheel of a one-way relationship? Will you change your name, will you cover your face, will you cut your hair and will you move in order to keep the ship afloat? Is this faith? Is this loyalty? Is this based on trust? Or are you naive, dear? Do you let people run you over, do what is expected of you, denying yourself?

This is why my friends think I’m insane.

entry.title: May Journal: Remember, Fly, and ILY (2025)

link.title: May Journal: Remember, Fly, and ILY (2025)

entry.content:
Remember

Fly

I Love You, Platonically

What the hell are these?

Collection of music videos I made for my friends birthdays because I was too broke to buy them something. It’s a fun challenge too, to try and compose one song in a week and animate a music video to accompany it. I did it 3 (technically 4) times and yet I only nailed the timeliness aspect once.

Who would’ve guessed, turns out animating and video editing take a long time! /s

entry.title: May Journal: Unfortunate Events (In Other Words I’m Stuck)

link.title: May Journal: Unfortunate Events (In Other Words I’m Stuck)

entry.content:
I do not want to talk about this day. I’m physically stuck and I’m mentally somewhere else. If there’s a silver lining at least I don’t die yet.

Hey, can we please stop looking at things as if they have a hidden lesson?

“Oh, you’re such a brave and stong kid for doing that! This surely taught you how to be an independent adult and you sure did go through it well!”

No. Can I just be pissed about this? None of these were not my fault. It didn’t teach me shit.

entry.title: May Journal: (if) everything ends
entry.content:
When the album does come, and in an unlikely event of it blowing up, the OG’s will remember that this song has long been published before the official release date!

If everything we ever had has come to and end, well I hope it ends in a good note
If this chapter of our lives has come to a close, well I don’t know, I wish I didn’t have to go

Cause I don’t want to be hurt
Yet I never learn
To put up a fight
And set my boundary right

Everything we ever called our home has always been a mess
So I bid my farewell and God bless.
